question: Who typically acts as the leader of a nursing team in the team nursing care delivery model?
explanation: In the team nursing model, a registered nurse is appointed as the team leader to oversee and coordinate patient care delivered by the group. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T4#GNS123_U1_T4_h1)

question: What is the primary purpose of developing the team nursing care delivery model?

options.A: To eliminate the need for registered nurses entirely
options.B: To address nursing shortages and improve patient satisfaction
options.C: To ensure doctors perform all bedside nursing procedures
options.D: To increase the cost of healthcare services

explanation: Team nursing was originally developed to tackle nursing shortages and enhance patient satisfaction through a decentralized, collaborative approach. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T4#GNS123_U1_T4_h1)

question: What is a primary goal of the team nursing model regarding professional staff?

options.A: To foster professional growth and mentorship for junior staff
options.B: To isolate junior staff from making clinical decisions
options.C: To ensure registered nurses perform all basic care tasks
options.D: To replace all auxiliary staff with doctors

explanation: The model aims to foster professional growth and mentorship by having junior staff and assistants work closely with experienced registered nurse leaders. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T4#GNS123_U1_T4_h2)

question: Which core principle is central to the philosophy of team nursing?

options.B: Maximization of each worker's scope of practice

explanation: Team nursing is built on collaboration, mutual respect, and maximizing each healthcare worker's specific scope of practice. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T4#GNS123_U1_T4_h2)

question: What is a primary responsibility of the Team Leader in team nursing?

options.A: Conducting initial patient assessments and developing care plans

explanation: The Team Leader is responsible for initial assessments, developing care plans, delegating tasks, and evaluating patient care outcomes. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T4#GNS123_U1_T4_h3)

question: Which tasks are typically assigned to nursing assistants in a team nursing setup?

options.C: Assisting patients with activities of daily living and baseline observations

explanation: Nursing assistants handle fundamental care activities like helping with daily living activities and taking basic observations within their training limits. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T4#GNS123_U1_T4_h3)

question: When is the team nursing conference or shift huddle typically held?

options.A: At the end of the work week
options.B: At the beginning of every shift

explanation: The team nursing conference is a structured meeting held at the beginning of every shift to review patients and allocate tasks. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T4#GNS123_U1_T4_h4)

question: What is one of the main benefits of the team nursing conference?

options.A: It allows junior staff and assistants to voice concerns and report observations
options.B: It completely replaces medical doctor rounds
options.C: It lengthens the duration of the shift unnecessarily
options.D: It prevents any need for documentation

explanation: The conference provides a platform for open dialogue where junior staff can voice concerns and report important patient observations. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T4#GNS123_U1_T4_h4)

question: What is a major advantage of the team nursing model?

options.B: Promotion of collaborative care and mentorship between experienced and junior staff
options.C: Ensuring every patient sees only one specific nurse forever
options.D: Removal of the need for registered nurses

explanation: Team nursing promotes collaborative care and fosters strong mentorship relationships between experienced nurses and junior staff. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T4#GNS123_U1_T4_h5)

question: What is a potential disadvantage associated with the team nursing model?

options.A: Guaranteed total elimination of medical errors
options.B: Fragmented care if communication breaks down among team members
options.C: Excessive independence where staff never work together
options.D: Complete lack of patient contact for all nurses

explanation: If communication breaks down among team members, care can become fragmented, which is a notable disadvantage of the model. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T4#GNS123_U1_T4_h5)

question: Which nursing care delivery model assigns 24-hour accountability to a single nurse for specific patients from admission to discharge?
explanation: Primary nursing establishes 24-hour accountability where one primary nurse manages patient care from admission to discharge. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T4#GNS123_U1_T4_h6)

question: How does functional nursing differ primarily from team nursing?

options.A: Functional nursing is strictly task-oriented, while team nursing focuses on holistic care through a collaborative team structure
options.B: Functional nursing uses only registered nurses, whereas team nursing uses no registered nurses
options.C: Functional nursing requires 24-hour accountability, unlike team nursing
options.D: Functional nursing has no role for nursing assistants

explanation: Functional nursing is heavily task-oriented and can be fragmented, whereas team nursing focuses on holistic, coordinated care led by a registered nurse. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T4#GNS123_U1_T4_h6)

question: Why is team nursing considered relevant in many Nigerian healthcare settings?

options.A: It eliminates the need for any nursing personnel
options.B: It optimizes the use of mixed cadres of nursing personnel to handle high patient-to-nurse ratios
options.C: It completely removes the problem of brain drain
options.D: It replaces doctors with nursing assistants

explanation: Team nursing is relevant in Nigeria because it optimizes mixed cadres of nursing staff to manage high patient-to-nurse ratios. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T4#GNS123_U1_T4_h7)

question: What is a major challenge to implementing team nursing in Nigerian hospitals?

options.A: An extreme surplus of registered nurses
options.B: Resource constraints, staff shortages due to brain drain, and hierarchical friction
options.C: The complete absence of patients in hospitals
options.D: Strict laws forbidding any form of task delegation

explanation: Implementation challenges include resource constraints, brain drain of experienced nurses, and hierarchical friction among staff cadres. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T4#GNS123_U1_T4_h7)
